validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated project. Trunkline Gas Company, LLC filed its application March 25, 2014 in Docket No. CP14-119-000 (with companion Dockets CP14-120-000 and CP14-122-000 for the affiliated Lake Charles Liquefaction/LNG dockets); FERC granted NGA Section 7(b)/(c) authorization for the Pipeline Modifications Project in its December 17, 2015 Order (153 FERC P61,300). Independently confirmed via EIA's federal Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (May 2026 release, 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' sheet, Excel row 101 -- exact-match row, same docket numbers) and DOE/FE's semi-annual status reports for the Lake Charles LNG Terminal (FE Docket No. 13-04-LNG, DOE/FE Order Nos. 3252 and 3868), which track this same Pipeline Modifications Project as part of one collectively-defined 'Project' with the Liquefaction Project. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- interstate NGA-certificated natural gas transmission facilities (EIA: Pipeline Type=Interstate, Authority=FERC; the order repeatedly describes 'natural gas' pipeline/compression/metering facilities), not a gathering or process line. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any other roster row -- no other of the 44 in-scope PIDs names Trunkline, the Mainline Connector, or the Mainline 200-3 Loop; P3663 (Commonwealth LNG) is a distinct terminal/pipeline system. ATTRIBUTION (ownership): Owner1='Trunkline Gas Co LLC' 100% is correct and independently confirmed (see Owner [ref] fill) -- Trunkline Gas Company, LLC is the FERC-certificate holder and the EIA workbook's own 'Pipeline Operator Name' field for this exact project.

validity.recommendation: Correct ConstructionYear to reflect when construction of this project's facilities actually began (FERC's Notice to Proceed with Construction, December 9, 2022), and note in ResearcherNotes that the 2024 date on the sheet is actually the IN-SERVICE date of a partial scope (compressor piping modifications), not a construction-start date, and that the row's primary physical scope (the mapped 11.4-mi/42-in Mainline Connector + 6.5-mi/24-in Mainline 200-3 Loop, i.e. the Length/Diameter this row records) had NOT begun construction as of the most recent DOE filing (April 2026) and remains pending Energy Transfer's final investment decision.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records ConstructionYear=2024. DOE's semi-annual Lake Charles LNG Terminal status report (April 1, 2026, FE Docket 13-04-LNG) gives the actual timeline: Trunkline requested FERC authorization to commence construction activities on November 23, 2022; FERC issued its Notice to Proceed with Construction on December 9, 2022, covering bi-directional-flow piping modifications at the Longville (Beauregard Parish, LA), Pollock (Grant Parish, LA), Shaw (Bolivar County, MS) and Epps (West Carroll Parish, LA) compressor stations. Trunkline filed its Request to Place Facilities In-Service December 11/18, 2023; FERC authorized commencement of service December 20, 2023; Trunkline's Notice of Commencement of Service confirms the modified facilities went into service January 1, 2024 -- i.e., 2024 is the IN-SERVICE date of that partial scope, not the year construction began (which was 2022). Crucially, this piping-modification scope is NOT the new-pipe segments this row's Length (18.00 mi) and Diameter (24, 42 in) describe -- those are the separate 11.4-mile/42-inch Mainline Connector and 6.5-mile/24-inch Mainline 200-3 Loop (FERC Order paragraph 19), and per the same DOE report and EIA's own notes ('project remains pending FID by Energy Transfer', EIA's May 2026 release, 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' sheet, Excel row 101), that new-pipe scope has NOT broken ground as of the April 2026 report. So the row's Status=construction/ConstructionYear=2024 conflates a small, already-built compressor-piping scope with the much larger new-pipe scope this row's own Length/Diameter/Capacity cells describe, which is still pre-construction. See the status_reviews entry for the recommended Status change to shelved given Energy Transfer's December 2025 suspension of the associated Lake Charles LNG development.

However, the PROJECT AS A WHOLE (the full Pipeline Modifications Project, which is what this GEM row represents) is genuinely multi-state: FERC's Order paragraph 20 states Trunkline also modifies its existing Mainline 100-3 pipeline via 'construction and modification of launcher/receiver barrels in Washington County, Mississippi, and Chicot County, Arkansas,' and DOE's April 2026 status report confirms bi-directional-flow piping modifications at the Shaw Compressor Station in Bolivar County, Mississippi (among others in Louisiana). EIA's own workbook (May 2026 release, 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' sheet, Excel row 101) records State(s)='AR,MS,LA' with Beg_State=AR, End_State=LA for this exact project. So: Mississippi IS a real, sourced facility location for this project (the Shaw Compressor Station piping modifications, Bolivar County) -- the sheet's StartState/Province='Mississippi' is not wrong. But Arkansas (the Chicot County launcher/receiver modification) is a third real facility state that the sheet's 2-slot Start/End schema cannot capture alongside Mississippi and Louisiana; this is a limitation of the schema for a compression/modification project spanning 3 states, not a factual error to correct. Per this batch's own rule ('a compression-only or multi-state project can legitimately touch states the new pipe does not'), no cell edit is proposed.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's Status=construction (last updated 2025-09-22, per this batch's roster) is now stale relative to a major, well-documented development: on December 18, 2025, Energy Transfer LP announced it is suspending development of the Lake Charles LNG export project, explicitly stating continued development 'is not warranted' and taking a $256 million impairment (SEC 10-K, FY2025, filed 2026-02-19). DOE's own semi-annual status report for the Lake Charles LNG Terminal (April 1, 2026) independently confirms the same December 18, 2025 suspension announcement and explicitly treats the Liquefaction Project and this Pipeline Modifications Project as ONE collectively-defined 'Project' subject to the same FERC completion deadline (extended to December 31, 2031) -- i.e., DOE's own filings do not distinguish the pipeline's fate from the terminal's. Two independent trade/local press sources (naturalgasintel.com, americanpress.com) corroborate the same December 2025 event contemporaneously. LNG-FEED-PIPELINE-FOLLOWS-TERMINAL CAVEAT: all four of these sources speak directly to the LAKE CHARLES LNG TERMINAL's suspension, not to a standalone announcement about the 'Trunkline Gas Pipeline' or 'Pipeline Modifications Project' by that name -- none of them name-check 'Trunkline' or 'Mainline Connector' when reporting the suspension (verified: url_verifier's --name check FAILED against 'Trunkline Gas Pipeline' for naturalgasintel.com and americanpress.com, and passed only when checked against 'Lake Charles LNG'). However, DOE's own report is the strongest available bridge: it is the SAME document (with the SAME DOE/FE docket) that separately, and in detail, discusses Trunkline's Pipeline Modifications Project construction history (piping mods in service Jan 2024, FERC extension to 2031) AND reports the December 2025 suspension in the same regulatory-activity log, treating both facts as part of one 'Project.' A DOE-sourced 8-K/businesswire press release URL cited BY the DOE report itself (businesswire.com/news/home/20251218689373/en/) could not be independently verified in this session (ReadTimeout on repeated attempts), so it is not used as a proposed_ref, but the same underlying fact is triple-corroborated by the SEC 10-K, the DOE report, and two press outlets. Given (a) the row's primary new-pipe scope has never begun construction and remains pre-FID per EIA's own notes, and (b) the sponsor has now suspended the entire collectively-defined Project (of which this pipeline is an integral, FERC-linked component) while remaining open to a future revival with a third party (not a permanent cancellation), 'shelved' (not 'cancelled') with ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed (this is a dated, sourced sponsor announcement, not a dormancy inference) is the best-supported status. ShelvedYear=2025 reflects the December 2025 announcement date.
